question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield close at or above 5.00% on 30 November 2026?
resolution_criteria: Yes if FRED series DGS10 for 2026-11-30 is >= 5.00. If 2026-11-30 has no observation, use the last observation before it.

reasoning.outside_view: Last close 5.15% (2026-11-13). Daily changes: sd 5.49bp over 60 days, 6.39bp over 20. A driftless random walk over the 10 remaining trading days (sd 17-20bp) gives 0.77-0.81 for staying at or above 5.00%. Over the last five years, 10-day falls of 15bp or more happened 17.7% of the time (base rate for No).
reasoning.decomposition: No requires a fall of more than 15bp in 10 trading days, around the Thanksgiving holiday, with the FOMC not meeting until December.
reasoning.inside_view: The Fed has been raising rates (effective funds rate 3.63% in August to 3.88% in October) and the 10-year rose 31bp in the week to 13 November, so the trend runs toward Yes; a sharp weekly jump also mean-reverts partly. These roughly cancel; shading slightly toward the empirical base rate.
reasoning.what_would_change_my_mind: A soft October CPI or payrolls surprise, or a 10bp+ daily rally, would move this toward 0.6; a further rise above 5.25% toward 0.9.
